criteria.text: Given a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL, when `POST /shorten` receives `{url}`, then it returns a success response containing unique non-empty `code` and `shortUrl` values.
Given malformed JSON, a missing URL, or an invalid/non-HTTP(S) URL, when `POST /shorten` is called, then it returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error response.
Given a generated code, when `GET /:code` is called, then it returns HTTP 302 with the original URL in the `Location` header.
Given an unknown code, when `GET /:code` is called, then it returns HTTP 404 with a JSON error response.
Given a generated code, when `GET /api/stats/:code` is called, then it returns `{code, url, hits, createdAt}` with an ISO-8601 creation timestamp.
Given an unknown code, when `GET /api/stats/:code` is called, then it returns HTTP 404 with a JSON error response.
Given repeated successful redirects, when statistics are requested, then `hits` equals the number of redirects performed and stats requests have not increased it.
Given multiple shortened URLs, when codes are generated, then no code overwrites or resolves to another entry.
Given a server restart, when prior codes are requested, then they are unavailable because storage is intentionally in-memory.
Given the standalone `createClient(baseUrl)` library, when consumers call `shorten`, `resolve`, or `stats`, then each method communicates with the API over HTTP and returns the corresponding result.
Given an API error or network failure, when a client-library method is called, then it rejects with actionable error information rather than returning a successful result.
Given the completed implementation, when its dependency manifest and runtime imports are inspected, then it uses only Node.js built-in modules and no external dependencies.
